plan.planning_summary: Refining route_03 (SiO2/Al2O3 multi-cavity UV bandpass filter) based on observed layer merging behavior. Four complementary routes address the merging issue through: (1) explicit spacer fixation and thickness diversity penalties, (2) alternative high-index material pair (HfO2/SiO2) for better index contrast, (3) reduced layer count with stronger cavity definition, and (4) systematic thickness grading to prevent collapse. All routes maintain the 255-280 nm passband and 300-1100 nm rejection objectives while preserving the ≤30 layer constraint.

routes.title: Constrained multi-cavity with fixed spacers and diversity penalty
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Fixing three central cavity spacer layers at exactly 67.5 nm while applying a thickness diversity penalty will prevent the layer merging observed in route_03, enabling distinct cavity resonances that improve UV passband transmission while maintaining visible/NIR rejection.
routes.design_principle: Multi-cavity bandpass filter with explicitly constrained spacer thicknesses and optimization bounds tightened around quarter-wave values at 267.5 nm center wavelength. Add cost penalty for consecutive layers with >95% thickness similarity.
routes.proposed_topology: 25 finite coating layers: Air | [SiO2/Al2O3]_12 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate. Three central spacer layers (layers 12, 13, 14) fixed at 67.5 nm.
design_variables: optimization bounds tightened to ±15% around quarter-wave targets
soft_objectives: maintain thickness diversity across adjacent layers
manufacturing_considerations: ALD or IAD deposition for thickness precision
quarter-wave layers at 267.5 nm approximately 45-70 nm depending on material index
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multi-cavity interference
Quarter-wave stack theory for high-reflectivity mirrors
Cavity resonance theory for bandpass transmission peaks
expected_advantages: Prevents layer merging collapse observed in route_03
Maintains distinct cavity resonances for sharper bandpass edges
Preserves the successful SiO2/Al2O3 material pair from route_03
known_risks: Fixed spacer thickness may limit optimization freedom
Diversity penalty may conflict with optimal physics solution
May still achieve similar target score if merging was not the primary limitation
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 25-layer SiO2/Al2O3 multi-cavity bandpass filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layers 1-25 alternate SiO2/Al2O3 starting with SiO2. Fix layers 12, 13, and 14 at exactly 67.5 nm thickness (non-optimizable). Optimize layers 1-11 and 15-25 with bounds ±15% around quarter-wave thickness at 267.5 nm center wavelength (SiO2 ~45 nm, Al2O3 ~67 nm). Apply optimization cost penalty of 0.01 per pair of consecutive layers with thickness similarity >95%. Wavelength bands: maximize transmittance 255-280 nm, minimize transmittance 300-700 nm, minimize transmittance 700-1100 nm. Total layer count exactly 25 finite coating layers. No metal layers. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with diversity constraint. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Directly addresses route_03 layer merging observation by fixing three central spacers at 67.5 nm and adding thickness diversity penalty per feedback directives. Maintains same material pair and layer count topology.

routes.title: HfO2/SiO2 material pair for higher index contrast
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Replacing Al2O3 with HfO2 as the high-index material will provide greater refractive index contrast (HfO2 n~2.0-2.2 vs Al2O3 n~1.6-1.7 in UV), enabling stronger stopband rejection with the same 25-layer count and potentially higher UV passband transmission.
routes.design_principle: Same multi-cavity topology as route_03 but with HfO2/SiO2 material pair. Literature evidence supports HfO2/SiO2 for UV filters with moisture-stable IAD deposition.
routes.proposed_topology: 25 finite coating layers: Air | [SiO2/HfO2]_12 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate. No fixed layers; all thicknesses optimizable.
design_variables: optimization bounds ±25% around quarter-wave targets at 267.5 nm
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 requires IAD for moisture stability and index homogeneity
HfO2 may exhibit thickness inhomogeneity without ion assistance
theory_basis: Higher index contrast produces wider stopbands for same layer count
HfO2 transparency in UV range with low absorption
IAD deposition produces dense, stable films
expected_advantages: Higher index contrast may improve stopband rejection without increasing layer count
HfO2/SiO2 system has literature precedent for UV filters
May achieve better target score than SiO2/Al2O3 with same topology
known_risks: HfO2 may have higher absorption near 255 nm than Al2O3
Material registry must support HfO2 optical constants in UV range
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 25-layer HfO2/SiO2 multi-cavity bandpass filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layers 1-25 alternate SiO2/HfO2 starting with SiO2. All 25 layer thicknesses optimizable with bounds ±25% around quarter-wave thickness at 267.5 nm center wavelength (SiO2 ~45 nm, HfO2 ~35 nm based on higher index). Wavelength bands: maximize transmittance 255-280 nm, minimize transmittance 300-700 nm, minimize transmittance 700-1100 nm. Total layer count exactly 25 finite coating layers. No metal layers. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer. Assume IAD deposition conditions for HfO2 optical constants. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Tests alternative material pair hypothesis while maintaining route_03's 25-layer multi-cavity topology. Addresses potential index contrast limitation of SiO2/Al2O3 system. Independent test of whether material selection rather than optimization constraints limited route_03 performance.

routes.title: Reduced 21-layer stack with stronger cavity definition
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count from 25 to 21 while maintaining three-cavity topology will reduce optimization complexity and layer merging tendency, allowing clearer cavity resonance definition and potentially better convergence to optimal thicknesses.
routes.design_principle: Simplified multi-cavity with fewer mirror pairs per cavity but same three-cavity structure. Fewer variables may reduce optimizer confusion and layer collapse.
routes.proposed_topology: 21 finite coating layers: Air | [SiO2/Al2O3]_3 | SiO2 (cavity 1) | [SiO2/Al2O3]_3 | SiO2 (cavity 2) | [SiO2/Al2O3]_3 | SiO2 (cavity 3) | [SiO2/Al2O3]_3 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate.
manufacturing_considerations: Fewer layers reduces deposition time and cumulative thickness error
Simpler stack may be more robust to thickness variations
ALD precision still required for cavity spacers
theory_basis: Multi-cavity bandpass theory with reduced mirror pair count
Optimization convergence improves with fewer variables
Cavity resonance strength depends on mirror reflectivity, not just layer count
expected_advantages: Reduced optimization complexity may prevent layer merging
Fewer layers reduces cumulative deposition error
May achieve comparable performance with simpler manufacturable stack
known_risks: Fewer mirror pairs may reduce stopband rejection strength
May not achieve same target score as 25-layer design
Three-cavity structure with fewer mirrors may have broader passband than desired
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 21-layer SiO2/Al2O3 three-cavity bandpass filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Topology: Air | (SiO2/Al2O3)×3 | SiO2 | (SiO2/Al2O3)×3 | SiO2 | (SiO2/Al2O3)×3 | SiO2 | (SiO2/Al2O3)×3 | SiO2 | Fused Silica. All 21 layer thicknesses optimizable with bounds ±20% around quarter-wave thickness at 267.5 nm center wavelength. Wavelength bands: maximize transmittance 255-280 nm, minimize transmittance 300-700 nm, minimize transmittance 700-1100 nm. Total layer count exactly 21 finite coating layers. No metal layers. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Tests whether route_03's 25-layer count contributed to optimization complexity and layer merging. Reduces variable count while preserving three-cavity topology. Independent test of layer count vs performance tradeoff.

routes.title: Graded thickness multi-cavity to prevent collapse
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses with systematic grading (varying quarter-wave target across the stack) rather than uniform quarter-wave will prevent the optimizer from collapsing layers to identical thicknesses, maintaining distinct optical functions for each layer.
routes.design_principle: Same 25-layer SiO2/Al2O3 topology as route_03 but with graded initial thicknesses: mirror layers near substrate use quarter-wave at longer wavelength (280 nm), mirror layers near air use quarter-wave at shorter wavelength (255 nm), creating natural thickness variation.
routes.proposed_topology: 25 finite coating layers: Air | [SiO2/Al2O3]_12 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate. All thicknesses optimizable but initialized with wavelength-graded quarter-wave targets.
design_variables: initialization uses graded quarter-wave from 255 nm to 280 nm across stack
manufacturing_considerations: Graded initialization may require more precise deposition control
Natural thickness variation may improve robustness to deposition errors
Same material pair as route_03 for direct comparison
theory_basis: Chirped mirror theory for broadband reflection
Thickness grading prevents degeneracy in optimization landscape
Multi-cavity filters benefit from asymmetric mirror design
expected_advantages: Prevents layer merging by design through graded initialization
May provide broader stopband rejection through chirped mirror effect
Maintains route_03 topology for direct performance comparison
known_risks: Graded design may complicate optimization convergence
May not significantly improve target score if merging was not the primary issue
Chirped mirrors may shift passband center wavelength
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 25-layer SiO2/Al2O3 multi-cavity bandpass filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layers 1-25 alternate SiO2/Al2O3 starting with SiO2. Initialize layer thicknesses with graded quarter-wave targets: layers 1-8 use quarter-wave at 255 nm, layers 9-17 use quarter-wave at 267.5 nm, layers 18-25 use quarter-wave at 280 nm. All 25 thicknesses optimizable with bounds ±20% around their respective initial values. Wavelength bands: maximize transmittance 255-280 nm, minimize transmittance 300-700 nm, minimize transmittance 700-1100 nm. Total layer count exactly 25 finite coating layers. No metal layers. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with graded initialization. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Tests initialization strategy as the cause of route_03 layer merging rather than constraint structure. Graded quarter-wave initialization provides natural thickness diversity without explicit penalties. Maintains same material pair and layer count for fair comparison.

research_influence: Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:199509322 supports SiO2/SiNx photonic crystal UV filter design with periodic (L/2 H L/2) units and AR coatings, informing multi-cavity topology in routes 04, 06, 07.
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:211025653 supports HfO2/SiO2 material pair for UV filters with IAD deposition, motivating route_05 material substitution.
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:16516444 supports ALD for precise thickness control in UV coatings, informing manufacturing considerations across all routes.

Route_03 observations (layer merging at ~67 nm, target score 0.296) directly motivated route_04's fixed spacer constraints and diversity penalty, route_06's reduced layer count, and route_07's graded initialization.
unresolved_decisions: Whether SiO2/Al2O3 or HfO2/SiO2 provides better UV transmission with adequate visible/NIR rejection remains untested.
Optimal layer count (21 vs 25) for balancing performance and manufacturability not yet determined.
Whether layer merging was caused by initialization, constraint structure, or optimizer dynamics requires comparison across routes 04, 06, 07.
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
